## Objective

Create and run source-only structural, focused, cross-package, and representative scenario checks without adopting the reusable sources into an active project.

## Scope

- Reusable source contract tests
- Conditional supporting-package regressions
- Skill validators and helper compilation
- Scenario matrix and evidence classification

## Entry conditions

- PHASE-003 is complete.
- All changed files and impact dispositions are available for review.

## Exit criteria

- Every changed package and role passes its applicable structural and focused checks.
- All required workflow scenarios have explicit observed outcomes.
- Verification limits remain source-only and truthful.

## Risks

- Static contract checks may not prove native runtime behavior.
- Validator environment differences must be reported rather than bypassed.

### Risks

- Static string checks alone could pass while the workflow contract remains contradictory.
- Tests could accidentally inspect active .agents copies instead of reusable sources.
- Test execution could create new __pycache__ residue.

### Acceptance criteria

- Focused tests cover root Director activation, Task identity, ownership, classification, all three paths, role selection and creation, solver independence, user overrides, one-to-one review, revision routing, synthesis, conflict recycling, ownership, completion evidence, audit records, state boundaries, and stop conditions.
- Cross-package tests verify every reference resolves to reusable source paths and conditional-package behavior matches the impact matrix.
- Tests use isolated temporary consumer fixtures where project-root context is needed and never overwrite active root or template files.
- Test limitations label native child execution and later consumer adoption as not exercised.

### Planned verification

- Run the new Task orchestration test module with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
- Run every affected existing package test module and the relevant repository contract tests.
- Inspect tests for source-path selection, temporary-directory isolation, meaningful failure modes, and no writes to protected paths.

### Risks

- The project virtual environment lacks PyYAML for the skill validator.
- A broad repository test can fail for a pre-existing unrelated dirty-tree expectation.
- Compilation or tests can create residue unless bytecode writes are disabled.

### Acceptance criteria

- The bundled skill validator passes for every changed skill package using the existing offline uv plus PyYAML route without installing into the project environment.
- Every affected focused unittest suite and applicable repository contract test passes with observed counts recorded.
- Every changed Python helper compiles and continues to use its approved dependency boundary.
- The reusable Project Director role contains every required operating section and all cross-package links resolve.
- Scoped git diff --check passes and any unrelated pre-existing failure is separated from regressions.

### Risks

- A source-only harness cannot establish consumer-project adoption or actual native multi-agent behavior.
- Scenario coverage could omit negative and no-progress cases while reporting an aggregate pass.

### Acceptance criteria

- The matrix separately passes the simple-direct, decomposed-complex, uncertain-adversarial, user-defined orchestration, one-to-one review, failed-review revision, all-pass synthesis, irreconcilable-conflict recycle, implementation-owner, evidence-gated completion, and no-progress blocker scenarios.
- Every scenario names its input, expected contract decisions, observed result, affected requirements, and verification level.
- No scenario mutates the active Task ledger, active skill copies, root guidance, the template project, or external state.
- Consumer adoption and live native child-agent execution remain explicitly not exercised unless later separately authorized and directly observed.

### Planned verification

- Run each scenario independently so one failure does not hide another.
- Compare scenario identifiers against REQ-001 through REQ-019 and report any uncovered requirement.
- Inspect temporary fixtures and post-run paths to prove active project files were not used as writable targets.
